key_insight: Thoracic aortic diameter and stiffness showed distinct circulating protein associations, suggesting different biological patterns underlying these imaging traits.
clinical_relevance: These findings may inform future aortic biomarker research but do not establish a screening test or treatment target.
method: Analyzed 2,920 circulating proteins in 6,773 UK Biobank participants with plasma proteomic and cardiac imaging data.
Tested associations with aortic diameter and pressure-free stiffness using multivariable regression and false discovery rate correction.
Explored biological pathways using ranked-protein enrichment and shared variation using secondary principal component analysis.
evidence_signal: Fully adjusted models identified 417 proteins associated with diameter and six with stiffness; the imaging traits were modestly correlated (r = 0.21).
watch_item: This observational aortic study—not AI cancer drug discovery—does not establish causality, and the supplied abstract is truncated.
paper_title: Distinct circulating proteomic patterns associated with thoracic aortic diameter and stiffness: A proteome-wide study in the UK Biobank
